title: Holding the Finance Function to Account
summary: Brings the programme together into a board question set for the CFO, auditors and finance function, and a practical plan for improving the board's financial oversight.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: Brings the programme together into a board question set for the CFO, auditors and finance function, and a practical plan for improving the board's financial oversight.
Learning Objectives: Assess the capability and independence of the finance function
Specify the financial and prudential information the board needs
Produce a personal and board action plan for financial oversight
Syllabus: Questions to ask the CFO: performance, capital, liquidity and judgements
Board financial and prudential management information
Seeing the numbers the way a supervisor does
Workshop: reviewing a board finance pack and agreeing actions
Intended Audience: Non-executive and independent directors without a finance or accounting background
Chairs and members of board committees other than audit, and newly appointed directors
Executive directors and senior managers from non-finance functions who sign off plans or returns
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Board or senior management experience in financial services is helpful. No accounting or finance qualification is required.
Core Reading: Basel Committee, The Basel Framework (consolidated Basel III standards)
Basel Committee, Principles for Sound Liquidity Risk Management and Supervision (2008)
IOSCO, Principles for the Valuation of Collective Investment Schemes (2013)
